history.dynasty: Ahom (rebuild); earliest structure speculated as 16th-century Koch
history.period: 1752 CE (Ahom rebuild by Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha); earliest founding uncertain
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is on Chitrachal (Navagraha) Hill in Guwahati proper - Silpukhuri/Chenikuthi/Chandmari area - NOT in Dispur, so the CSV town is wrong. It is an ancient temple whose exact founder is unknown; legend attributes the earliest structure to the Koch kings (16th century), it suffered extensive damage in the great earthquake of 1697, and was rebuilt by Ahom king Rajeswar Singha in 1752 (per a temple inscription). The sanctum holds nine Graha Lingams (Shiva lingams representing the nine celestial bodies), each covered with a coloured garment symbolic of its planet, a rare arrangement. The nine-cornered (na-kunia) Silpukhuri tank was dug in the valley south of the temple. Renovations are reported for 1923-1945 (verify). Coordinates are geocoded for Navagraha Road, Chenikuthi (Silpukhuri), corroborated by Wikipedia's 26.19092, 91.76525.

name: Navagraha Temple
town: Guwahati (CSV town 'Dispur' is WRONG - the temple is on Navagraha Hill at Silpukhuri/Chandmari)
town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and the main gateway to Northeast India, set on the banks of the Brahmaputra river. It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in India (ancient Pragjyotishpura) and hosts several major temples including Kamakhya, Navagraha and Umananda.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport - about 25 km (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati Junction railway station - about 3-4 km (verify).
travel.road: On Navagraha Hill (Navagraha Road), Chenikuthi/Silpukhuri area, reachable by auto and private vehicles from any part of Guwahati.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; hilltop gives panoramic views of Guwahati.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not consistently documented across sources (verify). Remove footwear; expect a climb to the hilltop shrine.
